#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby incremental code indexing after checkout
if [ "$3" = "1" ] && [ -n "$1" ] && [ -n "$2" ]; then
    if git rev-parse -q --verify "$1^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null)
    else
        CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r "$2" 2>/dev/null)
    fi
else
    CHANGED_FILES=
fi
if [ -n "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
    GCODE="${GOBBY_HOME:-$HOME/.gobby}/bin/gcode"
    if [ -x "$GCODE" ]; then
        # Waits for a busy index lock instead of skipping: a skipped run exits 3 and
        # nothing retries it. The wait runs in the background, so the commit never blocks,
        # and it is capped at 300 s so waiters from successive commits cannot pile up.
        (
            echo "$CHANGED_FILES" | sed 's/^/--files=/' | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 "$GCODE" index --quiet --lock-wait-seconds 300 >/dev/null 2>&1
        ) &
    fi
fi
# <<< GOBBY HOOK END <<<

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby incremental code indexing after merge
if git rev-parse -q --verify ORIG_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # $1 is 1 for a squash merge: it moves no HEAD, so the staged worktree holds its changes.
    if [ "$1" != "1" ] && [ "$(git rev-parse ORIG_HEAD)" != "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ]; then
        CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only ORIG_HEAD HEAD 2>/dev/null)
    else
        CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only HEAD 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -z "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
            CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r HEAD 2>/dev/null)

else

fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby incremental code indexing after rewrite
REWRITE_LINES=$(cat)
CHANGED_FILES=$(
    printf '%s\n' "$REWRITE_LINES" | while read -r OLD_REV NEW_REV; do
        if [ -n "$OLD_REV" ] && [ -n "$NEW_REV" ]; then
            git diff --name-only "$OLD_REV" "$NEW_REV" 2>/dev/null
        fi
    done | sort -u
)
if [ -n "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
    GCODE="${GOBBY_HOME:-$HOME/.gobby}/bin/gcode"
    if [ -x "$GCODE" ]; then
        # Waits for a busy index lock instead of skipping: a skipped run exits 3 and
        # nothing retries it. The wait runs in the background, so the commit never blocks,
        # and it is capped at 300 s so waiters from successive commits cannot pile up.
        (
            echo "$CHANGED_FILES" | sed 's/^/--files=/' | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 "$GCODE" index --quiet --lock-wait-seconds 300 >/dev/null 2>&1
        ) &
    fi
fi
# Hand the captured stdin to hook content chained after this section through a
# pipe. The PID check runs the replay once even if the end marker is misplaced.
if [ -n "$REWRITE_LINES" ] && [ "${GOBBY_CHAINED_PID:-}" != "$$" ]; then
    GOBBY_CHAINED=$(sed '1,/^# [<][<][<] GOBBY HOOK END [<][<][<]$/d' "$0") || exit 1
    if [ -n "$GOBBY_CHAINED" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$REWRITE_LINES" | {
            GOBBY_CHAINED_PID=$$
            eval "$GOBBY_CHAINED
"
        }
        exit
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby smart pre-commit wrapper
# - Runs gobby verification commands (if configured)
# - Runs pre-commit framework if available
# - Restages auto-fixes into the in-progress commit; never commits on its own
# - Task/memory JSONL sync moved to pre-push
# - Never stashes: pre-commit runs on the staged paths only (--files). Its default
#   stash checks out every unstaged path in the checkout and restores them after
#   the hooks, which dropped or rolled back concurrent writes from other sessions.
#   Hooks that take filenames see only the staged paths; hooks that take none see
#   the live checkout. A fixer that rewrites a partially staged path edits its
#   unstaged hunks in place, and the wrapper then refuses the commit without
#   restaging it. A write by another session during the hook makes pre-commit report
#   a modified file; the wrapper ignores paths outside the staged set and re-runs
#   the hooks. With no staged paths to check, pre-commit is skipped rather than
#   run without files, which would stash. Names are read NUL-delimited, so git
#   never C-quotes a name with " or \ into a literal pre-commit cannot find. A
#   changed path whose name contains a newline is refused, because no line list can
#   carry it. A commit that only deletes paths has no file to check, so pre-commit
#   is skipped there and always_run hooks do not fire.

# Run Gobby verification commands for pre-commit stage
if command -v gobby >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gobby hooks run pre-commit 2>/dev/null
    GOBBY_EXIT=$?
    if [ $GOBBY_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "Gobby pre-commit verification failed"
        exit $GOBBY_EXIT
    fi
fi

# Run pre-commit if available and config exists
if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ]; then
    # POSIX sh: path sets go through files in a scratch directory. The subshell
    # owns its EXIT trap, so cleanup never replaces a trap of chained hook content.
    (
    # macOS bare mktemp ignores TMPDIR; use the sandbox's writable temp explicitly.
    GOBBY_SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gobby-pre-commit.XXXXXX") || exit 1
    trap 'rm -rf "$GOBBY_SCRATCH"' EXIT

    # git reads GIT_INDEX_FILE, the index this commit is built from, so plain,
    # -a, and path-limited commits each snapshot and restage their own path set.
    # -z keeps each name raw; tr turns the list into lines for the commands below.
    _gobby_paths() {
        git diff -z --name-only --ignore-submodules "$@" | LC_ALL=C tr '\0' '\n' | LC_ALL=C sort
    }
    # "<worktree blob> <path>" for each unstaged path, to see what pre-commit rewrote
    _gobby_worktree_states() {
        _gobby_paths --diff-filter=d >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/paths"
        [ -s "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/paths" ] || return 0
        # A quote-leading path triggers git's C-unquoting. Prefix only the hash
        # inputs; the original names still identify paths in the state records.
        sed 's|^|./|' "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/paths" >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/hash-paths"
        git hash-object --stdin-paths <"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/hash-paths" \
            >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/blobs" || return 1
        paste -d ' ' "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/blobs" "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/paths" | LC_ALL=C sort
    }

    # A newline would split one name into two fragments, and pre-commit would check
    # the wrong files. Refuse before any hook runs; nothing is restaged or committed.
    { git diff --cached -z --name-only --ignore-submodules
      git diff -z --name-only --ignore-submodules
    } | LC_ALL=C tr -cd '\n' >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/newline-names"
    if [ -s "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/newline-names" ]; then
        echo ""
        echo "Gobby pre-commit cannot check a changed path whose name contains a newline."
        echo "Rename that path, then retry. Nothing was committed."
        exit 1
    fi

    _gobby_paths --cached >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/staged-before"
    _gobby_paths >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/unstaged-before"
    _gobby_worktree_states >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/states-before" || exit 1

    # Explicit files keep pre-commit from stashing; a deleted path has no file to check.
    # A commit that only deletes paths runs no hooks here (see the header).
    _gobby_paths --cached --diff-filter=d >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/framework-paths"
    set --
    while IFS= read -r GOBBY_PATH; do
        set -- "$@" "$GOBBY_PATH"
    done <"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/framework-paths"
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || exit 0

    pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit --files "$@"
    PRECOMMIT_EXIT=$?

    if [ $PRECOMMIT_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
        _gobby_worktree_states >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/states-after" || exit 1
        CHANGED=$(LC_ALL=C comm -13 "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/states-before" \
            "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/states-after" | cut -d ' ' -f 2- | LC_ALL=C sort)
        # Only staged paths can be fixes. A changed path outside the staged set was
        # written by another session during the hook; pre-commit reports it as a
        # modified file, so it is never restaged and the hooks are re-run instead.
        AUTO_FIXED=$(printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | LC_ALL=C comm -12 - "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/framework-paths")
        if [ -z "$AUTO_FIXED" ]; then
            [ -n "$CHANGED" ] || exit $PRECOMMIT_EXIT
            pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit --files "$@"
            exit $?
        fi

        # A fix may join the commit only if its path was fully staged; anything
        # else would sweep unstaged hunks or unstaged paths into the commit.
        LC_ALL=C comm -23 "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/staged-before" "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/unstaged-before" \
            >"$GOBBY_SCRATCH/fully-staged"
        NOT_RESTAGEABLE=$(printf '%s\n' "$AUTO_FIXED" |
            LC_ALL=C comm -23 - "$GOBBY_SCRATCH/fully-staged")
        if [ -n "$NOT_RESTAGEABLE" ]; then
            echo ""
            echo "Pre-commit auto-fixed files that were not fully staged:"
            printf '%s\n' "$NOT_RESTAGEABLE" | sed 's/^/  /'
            echo "Nothing was restaged. Stage the fixes that belong in this commit, then retry."
            exit 1
        fi

        echo ""
        echo "Pre-commit auto-fixed staged files. Restaging the fixes into this commit..."
        printf '%s\n' "$AUTO_FIXED" | tr '\n' '\0' |
            git --literal-pathspecs add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul || exit 1

        # A path-limited commit is built from a temporary index while git holds
        # the caller's real index at index.lock, to install after the commit.
        # Restage there too so the caller's index keeps the committed fixes.
        REAL_INDEX=$(unset GIT_INDEX_FILE; git rev-parse --git-path index)
        if [ -n "${GIT_INDEX_FILE:-}" ] && [ -f "$REAL_INDEX.lock" ] \
            && ! [ "$GIT_INDEX_FILE" -ef "$REAL_INDEX" ] \
            && ! [ "$GIT_INDEX_FILE" -ef "$REAL_INDEX.lock" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$AUTO_FIXED" | tr '\n' '\0' | GIT_INDEX_FILE="$REAL_INDEX.lock" \
                git --literal-pathspecs add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul || exit 1
        fi

        # Re-run so failures pre-commit could not fix still block the commit
        pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-commit --files "$@" || exit $?
    fi
    ) || exit $?
fi
# <<< GOBBY HOOK END <<<

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby verification runner for pre-merge-commit
# Skip when Gobby itself is performing a merge (e.g. merge_clone)
if [ "$GOBBY_MERGE" != "1" ]; then
    # Runs configured verification commands (code_review, integration tests, etc.)
    if command -v gobby >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        gobby hooks run pre-merge
        GOBBY_EXIT=$?
        if [ $GOBBY_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Gobby pre-merge-commit verification failed"
            exit $GOBBY_EXIT
        fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby verification runner for pre-push
# Runs configured verification commands (type_check, unit_tests, security, etc.)

# Capture pre-push refs once for delete-only checks.
PUSH_REFS=$(cat)
ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"

DELETE_ONLY=false
# A pipe, not a here-document (see _restore_stdin). The loop exits 1 at the
# first ref that pushes a commit.
if [ -n "$PUSH_REFS" ] && printf '%s\n' "$PUSH_REFS" |
    while read -r local_ref local_sha _; do
        if [ -n "$local_ref" ] && [ "$local_sha" != "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
            exit 1
        fi
    done
then
    DELETE_ONLY=true
fi
if [ "$DELETE_ONLY" != true ]; then
    # Gobby backup — snapshot tasks and memories outside the repository before push
    # Skip for spawned agents to avoid JSONL contamination in worktrees
    if [ -z "$GOBBY_AGENT_RUN_ID" ] && command -v gobby >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        gobby tasks backup --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
        gobby memory backup --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

    if command -v gobby >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        gobby hooks run pre-push 2>/dev/null
        GOBBY_EXIT=$?
        if [ $GOBBY_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Gobby pre-push verification failed"
            exit $GOBBY_EXIT
        fi
    fi
fi

# Hand the captured stdin to hook content chained after this section through a
# pipe. The PID check runs the replay once even if the end marker is misplaced.
if [ -n "$PUSH_REFS" ] && [ "${GOBBY_CHAINED_PID:-}" != "$$" ]; then
    GOBBY_CHAINED=$(sed '1,/^# [<][<][<] GOBBY HOOK END [<][<][<]$/d' "$0") || exit 1
    if [ -n "$GOBBY_CHAINED" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$PUSH_REFS" | {
            GOBBY_CHAINED_PID=$$
            eval "$GOBBY_CHAINED
"
        }
        exit
    fi
fi
exec 0</dev/null
# <<< GOBBY HOOK END <<<

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# >>> GOBBY HOOK START >>>
# Gobby protected-branch guard. The branch checked out in the main worktree
# takes code through gobby-tasks-ops:land_commit unless its committed project
# marker enables allow_direct_integration_commits. Otherwise the update needs the
# committing session's grant: ghook asks the daemon, and only an allow verdict lands.
# POSIX sh; JSON parsing uses the stdlib of the python3 on PATH when the hook runs.
# The installing interpreter is never baked in: a managed run's environment is
# removed with its cache, and the hook would then refuse every protected update.
GOBBY_REF_LINES=$(cat)
gobby_refuse() {
    echo "Gobby refused the update of ${GOBBY_PROTECTED_REF:-the protected branch}: $1." >&2
    echo "Code lands through gobby-tasks-ops:land_commit (operator override: GOBBY_LAND_COMMIT=1)." >&2
    exit 1
}
gobby_python() {
    command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || gobby_refuse "python3 is not on PATH"
    python3 "$@"
}
GOBBY_PROTECTED_REF=
if [ "$1" = "prepared" ] && [ "${GOBBY_LAND_COMMIT:-}" != "1" ]; then
    GOBBY_COMMON_DIR=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) ||
        gobby_refuse "cannot find the main checkout"
    # git reads HEAD in every ref format (a reftable HEAD file is a stub). Status 1 is
    # a detached HEAD, which protects nothing; any other failure refuses.
    GOBBY_PROTECTED_REF=$(git --git-dir="$GOBBY_COMMON_DIR" symbolic-ref -q HEAD)
    case $? in
    0|1) ;;
    *) gobby_refuse "cannot resolve the main checkout's HEAD" ;;
    esac
fi
if [ -n "$GOBBY_PROTECTED_REF" ]; then
    # Pipes, not here-documents (see _restore_stdin). gobby_refuse exits only its
    # pipeline's subshell, so each pipeline passes the refusal on.
    printf '%s\n' "$GOBBY_REF_LINES" | while read -r gobby_old gobby_new gobby_ref; do
        if [ "$gobby_ref" = "ORIG_HEAD" ]; then
            # merge/pull save ORIG_HEAD before rewriting the index and
            # worktree. Refusing their later branch update cannot undo that
            # rewrite. This transaction has no incoming target to classify, so
            # even allowed-path merges must use the landing path. Resolve the
            # caller's HEAD too: a lane's ORIG_HEAD must remain unrestricted.
            gobby_checkout_ref=$(git symbolic-ref -q HEAD)
            case $? in
            0|1) ;;
            *) gobby_refuse "cannot resolve the current checkout's HEAD" ;;
            esac
            if [ "$gobby_checkout_ref" = "$GOBBY_PROTECTED_REF" ]; then
                gobby_checkout_dir=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) ||
                    gobby_refuse "cannot find the current checkout's git directory"
                # worktree add populates HEAD under a lock before creating its
                # first ORIG_HEAD. Allow only that clean initialization; a
                # populated locked worktree already has ORIG_HEAD.
                if [ "$gobby_checkout_dir" != "$GOBBY_COMMON_DIR" ] &&
                    [ -f "$gobby_checkout_dir/locked" ] &&
                    ! git rev-parse -q --verify ORIG_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
                    git diff-index --cached --quiet HEAD -- && git diff-files --quiet --
                then
                    continue
                fi
                gobby_refuse "checkout-changing operations cannot update ORIG_HEAD directly"
            fi
        fi
        [ "$gobby_ref" = "$GOBBY_PROTECTED_REF" ] || continue
        case $gobby_new in
        *[!0]*) ;;
        *)
            # pack-refs prunes the loose copy of a ref it has just packed: the old
            # value is already in packed-refs, and unlike every real deletion it
            # holds no packed-refs lock while the hook runs.
            if [ ! -e "$GOBBY_COMMON_DIR/packed-refs.lock" ] &&
                grep -qxF "$gobby_old $gobby_ref" "$GOBBY_COMMON_DIR/packed-refs" 2>/dev/null
            then
                continue
            fi
            gobby_refuse "the protected branch cannot be deleted" ;;
        esac
        # A zero old value is a creation or a forced update; read the ref to tell.
        case $gobby_old in
        *[!0]*) ;;
        *) gobby_old=$(git --no-replace-objects rev-parse -q --verify "$gobby_ref^{commit}") ||
            continue ;;
        esac
        # Only the policy already landed on the protected branch can authorize
        # an update. The index, worktrees and incoming commit are not authority.
        gobby_marker=$(git --no-replace-objects ls-tree "$gobby_old" -- .gobby/project.json) ||
            gobby_refuse "cannot locate the committed project policy"
        if [ -n "$gobby_marker" ]; then
            # Preserve the blob bytes: shell substitution would strip NULs.
            gobby_python -I -S -c '
import json, subprocess, sys
try:
    project = json.loads(subprocess.check_output([
        "git", "--no-replace-objects", "show", sys.argv[1] + ":.gobby/project.json"
    ]))
except (ValueError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
    sys.exit(2)
if not isinstance(project, dict):
    sys.exit(2)
policy = project.get("allow_direct_integration_commits", False)
if type(policy) is not bool:
    sys.exit(2)
sys.exit(0 if policy else 1)
' "$gobby_old"
            case $? in
            0) continue ;;
            1) ;; # False or an absent key retains the path allowance.
            *) gobby_refuse "invalid or unreadable allow_direct_integration_commits policy" ;;
            esac
        fi
        # Unquoted non-ASCII matches the policy; git still quotes control characters.
        gobby_paths=$(git --no-replace-objects -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-only --no-renames \
            "$gobby_old" "$gobby_new") ||
            gobby_refuse "cannot list the paths changed by $gobby_old..$gobby_new"
        # An update that changes no path carries no content for the verdict to judge.
        [ -n "$gobby_paths" ] || continue
        gobby_branch=${gobby_ref#refs/heads/}
        # ghook asks the daemon for the committing session's verdict. Only an allow lands.
        # A missing session or ghook, a failed run, or an unreadable verdict refuses.
        # The interpreter gets its own stdin, so the ref-line loop keeps its input.
        gobby_python -I -S -c '
import json, os, subprocess, sys
branch, joined = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
session = os.environ.get("GOBBY_SESSION_ID", "")
ghook = os.path.join(os.environ.get("HOME", ""), ".gobby", "bin", "ghook")
if not session or not os.access(ghook, os.X_OK):
    print("the committing session or ghook is unavailable", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
payload = {
    "session_id": session,
    "cwd": os.getcwd(),
    "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
    "tool_name": "Bash",
    "tool_input": {"command": "git commit"},
    "staged_paths": [path for path in joined.split("\n") if path],
    "integration_branch": branch,
}
try:
    verdict = subprocess.run(
        [ghook, "--gobby-owned", "--cli=git", "--type=PreToolUse"],
        input=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        capture_output=True,
        timeout=60,
    )
except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
    print(f"ghook returned no verdict: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
body = verdict.stdout.decode(errors="replace").strip()
granted = verdict.returncode == 0
if body:
    try:
        granted = granted and json.loads(body).get("decision") == "allow"
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        granted = False
sys.stderr.write(verdict.stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
sys.exit(0 if granted else 1)
' "$gobby_branch" "$gobby_paths" ||
            gobby_refuse "the committing session's grant does not cover this update"
    done || exit 1
fi

# Hand the captured stdin to hook content chained after this section through a
# pipe. The PID check runs the replay once even if the end marker is misplaced.
if [ -n "$GOBBY_REF_LINES" ] && [ "${GOBBY_CHAINED_PID:-}" != "$$" ]; then
    GOBBY_CHAINED=$(sed '1,/^# [<][<][<] GOBBY HOOK END [<][<][<]$/d' "$0") || exit 1
    if [ -n "$GOBBY_CHAINED" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$GOBBY_REF_LINES" | {
            GOBBY_CHAINED_PID=$$
            eval "$GOBBY_CHAINED
"
        }
        exit
    fi
fi
exec 0</dev/null
# <<< GOBBY HOOK END <<<
